comment: Sex is a story, not an action.
A quickie in an alley is one stage and it is over. Sex at home has a prelude,
a middle and a finish, and each of those is a ROLE rather than a named
animation -- a prelude might be a handjob, a blowjob or cunnilingus, and which
one happens should depend on what the packs supply, not on this file.
HOW A SCENE IS ACTUALLY STAGED: by AAF, not by us.
This file used to say a stage moves the scene along with AAF's ChangePosition.
It does not. ChangePosition was refused 26 times out of 26 -- with tag filters,
with a named position id, and with no filters at all. The last of those is what
settles it: a call asking for nothing in particular is still refused, so no tag
list here can fix it.
What DOES work is StartScene, which honours a named position -- and a position
may declare positionTree="...", so naming a position IS choosing a tree. AAF
then walks that tree to its own ending on the pack author's own timings.
So: ONE TREE PER SCENE, chosen when the scene starts. A stage is now a MOOD --
its face, for its share of the story -- and asks AAF for nothing at all. Stage
seconds are WEIGHTS, scaled onto however long the chosen tree is really
authored for, because nobody writing this file can know that number.
WHO CHOOSES a scenario: not Rapport. The framework executes one an addon names
through Core.RequestScene. Rapport's own scheduler names one only because it is
standing in for Chemistry until Chemistry exists, and it says so in the code.
comment_stages: seconds  this stage's WEIGHT, not a promise. Nothing imposes a length on a
scene any more: it lasts as long as its author made it. These numbers
are rescaled onto the chosen tree's real length so the faces land in
proportion. If no tree was chosen they are used as written.
include  on a tree stage, the kind of ENDING wanted. Any one of them matches.
Matched against the position the tree ends ON, not the one it starts
on -- 54 of the 74 tree-bearing positions on this install carry
different tags at the two ends, so a tree that opens doggy can end in
a facial and asking for either used to get the other.
exclude  tags to avoid, tested at BOTH ends. A tag you do not want is not
acceptable merely because the tree saves it for last.
tree     true means THIS is the stage that chooses the scene's tree. The last
such stage wins. A scenario with no tree stage starts unconstrained:
AAF picks freely, which is right for a quickie and may be short.
Inferring this from include being non-empty is what once handed
quickie a six-stage climax tree.
requireEnding  default true: prefer trees that reach a climax or an orgasm.
A PREFERENCE, not a wall -- when nothing both matches and is graded,
a matching ungraded tree is taken and the log says so loudly.
handover true means this stage asks AAF for nothing and lets what is already
playing carry on. Every stage does that now, so this is a no-op kept
for older files.
face     the Rapport expression set for this stage. Expressions follow the
STORY, not a percentage of the clock: a percentage cannot know that
40% of this scene is still foreplay.
KNOWN GAP: two women get no tree. AAF's packs ship 24 female/female positions
here and not one declares a positionTree, so an f_f pair always starts
unconstrained however this file is written. They play; nothing can promise how
they end. Core.CanRun reports that rather than pretending.
